messages:
sophie: Quick question about auth behavior after a key rotation — saw a customer report where requests with an OLD key + correct X-Project-Id now return 403 instead of 401. I thought rotated/invalid keys should be 401. Is that expected or a regression? @devin

devin: Hmm. We used to return 401 for expired/invalid keys and 403 when a valid key lacked project access. Could be a check-order issue in the middleware. What's the exact client flow?

sophie: They rotate keys via the console -> SDK keeps sending old key for a short window -> header `X-Project-Id: proj_abc` included -> response 403 body: "forbidden: project mismatch". Expected 401. Causing SDK to surface wrong error.

maya: From product POV, 401 makes more sense for "invalid/rotated" because it signals re-auth. 403 implies permission problem which confuses error handling. :+1:

devin: Looking at auth middleware quick (local copy):

```
// simplified pseudo
key = lookupKey(authHeader)
if (!key) return 401
if (key.projectId != headers['X-Project-Id']) return 403
if (key.state == 'rotated' || key.expired) return 401
// allow
```

That ordering will return 403 for an old key if the project check runs before state check.

tyler: We intentionally moved project-scope check earlier in a 2025-11 deploy to reduce attack surface from probing keys across projects. See PR #345. Might have introduced this behavior.

devin: Right — security rationale was to avoid leaking whether a key exists for a different project. But returning 403 for rotated/expired keys still leaks similar info. Better to validate key state first, then scope.

maya: If we change order, do we re-open any user-enumeration vectors? @sec sign-off needed. But product impact (wrong error surfaced) is real.

devin: Proposed fix (pseudo):

```
key = lookupKey(authHeader)
if (!key) return 401
if (key.state == 'rotated' || key.expired) return 401
if (key.projectId != headers['X-Project-Id']) return 403
// allow
```

This keeps rotated/expired keys returning 401. It still avoids revealing key existence for totally missing keys.

auth-bot: FYI deploy v1.43 rolled on 2025-11-02 by @tyler (change: move project-check earlier).

tyler: We can add a short canary and update the auth docs to clarify: "compat: requests with rotated/expired keys will return 401 regardless of X-Project-Id". Also add an integration test.

maya: Sounds good. Please include a note for SDK teams so they know to treat 401 as "reauth needed" and 403 as "access denied to project".

sophie: I'll file a tiny RFC + acceptance criteria and ping @sec for review. Can we also add a small log metric for "auth:old-key-received" so support can correlate rotation events?

devin: Will open PR with tests + metric. I'll target canary on eng-oncall first.

sophie: Awesome — thx. @tyler can you link PR and canary plan here once ready? :thumbsup:
